harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on CentOS Stream 10, exercised a full failover (node1 lost -> node2 promoted -> node3 repointed -> node1 rejoined as standby of node2) with zero data loss, and completed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes with proof of changed boot identity and full post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server/contrib 16.14 on node1, node2, node3 via dnf
Initialized DB on node1; configured wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, hot_standby, and pg_hba.conf for replication and client access
Generated the replicator role's password on node1 with openssl and passed it to other nodes only via secret_env, never in literal command text
Opened firewalld postgresql service on all three nodes
Built node2 and node3 as standbys via pg_basebackup -R from node1; verified standby.signal/primary_conninfo and confirmed streaming state with ~0 replication lag
Created a test table and inserted baseline rows; confirmed replication to both standbys
Simulated primary loss: confirmed node2 fully caught up to node1's WAL LSN, then stopped postgresql on node1
Promoted node2 to writable primary via pg_ctl promote; verified zero data loss (all pre-failover rows present) and that new writes succeed on node2
Repointed node3's primary_conninfo to node2 and restarted it as a standby of the new primary; verified streaming and full data consistency
Rebuilt node1 via pg_basebackup -R from node2 and started it as a standby of node2; verified recovery mode and intact data
Captured boot_id and health baseline on all three nodes
Rebooted node1, then node3, then node2 (the primary) one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling each node until exec access returned
Proved each restart via changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id (not just elapsed time or service state)
Verified post-restart recovery for each node: node1 and node3 resumed streaming as standbys with full data; node2 resumed as writable primary, accepted a new write, and both standbys replicated it

evidence.summary: postgresql installed and initialized on node1; replication settings and replicator role created; node2/node3 built via pg_basebackup -R with standby.signal and primary_conninfo pointing at node1; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both standbys streaming

evidence.requirement: Replicated data verified consistent before disruption
evidence.summary: Rows inserted on node1 primary appear identically on node2 and node3 standbys

evidence.requirement: Primary loss simulated and standby promoted without data loss
evidence.summary: node2 confirmed at matching WAL LSN before node1 was stopped; node2 promoted to primary (pg_is_in_recovery=f) and accepted a new write while retaining all prior rows including the last one written on node1 pre-failover

evidence.requirement: Remaining standby (node3) repointed to new primary
evidence.summary: node3 primary_conninfo updated to node2, restarted, confirmed streaming from node2 in pg_stat_replication and holding the post-failover row

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary (node1) rejoins as standby of current primary (node2)
evidence.summary: node1 rebuilt via pg_basebackup -R from node2, started as standby (pg_is_in_recovery=t) with full data, and node2's pg_stat_replication shows both node1 and node3 streaming

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4d340bf4...; systemctl reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 9c54dcf4... (changed); postgresql active, standby recovery mode confirmed, all rows present, node2 shows node1 streaming again

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4d842549...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 26c0dbdc... (changed); postgresql active, standby recovery mode confirmed, all rows present, node2 shows node3 streaming again

evidence.requirement: node2 (primary) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state as primary
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id cce73776...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id abf60f22... (changed); postgresql resumed active as writable primary (pg_is_in_recovery=f), accepted a new write, and both node1 and node3 replicated the new row, proving full cluster recovery

attempts.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on CentOS Stream 10, exercised a full failover (node1 lost -> node2 promoted -> node3 repointed -> node1 rejoined as standby of node2) with zero data loss, and completed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes with proof of changed boot identity and full post-restart recovery.
